help.errors_1: Error key:xxx is not mapped to any known key: the key name is not in the table above. Check the spelling (the table is case-insensitive) and join combinations with +.
help.errors_10: text: types strange characters: the active input method affects it; switch to an English input method before running, and use paste: for Chinese text or symbols.
help.errors_11: paste: does nothing or pastes stale content: look for "clipboard unavailable, paste step skipped" in the log. On Linux install xclip (X11) or wl-copy (Wayland), or use the tkinter fallback under a graphical session. If password fields still fail, work through "What to do when password fields ignore input" above.
help.errors_12: app: starts but text goes to another window: desktop apps start slower than browsers, so within the 3 s window (Windows) the app may not have focus yet. Add wait:1000 before the following text: / key: steps; if that does not help, the app may be opening in the background or be blocked by UAC. macOS/Linux never waits after app:, so always add a wait: there.
help.errors_13: app: reports "executable not found": the path is wrong or the exe is not there. Quote paths with spaces, e.g. app:"C:\Program Files\App\app.exe"; a bare name such as app:notepad must be on PATH; environment variables work too, e.g. app:%LOCALAPPDATA%\App\app.exe.
help.errors_14: app: reports "unbalanced quotes in the command line": the quotes do not pair up (one extra " or '). Nothing is launched, the step is skipped and later steps still run. Count the quotes in the path or arguments, e.g. app:"C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" --title="My App".
help.errors_2: Nothing happens and the card is breathing: the action is still running (the card border brightens and "Test action" turns into a red "Stop"). Repeated presses are ignored while it runs and the log only shows one "Action skipped" row. It recovers when the macro ends; "Stop" on the card quits at the next step boundary, and keys already sent are not taken back.
help.errors_3: The macro does nothing at all: macros need the keyboard package (pip install keyboard; the Windows build bundles it). Make sure Host actions is enabled under Device → Device and host, that the action type is Macro, and that Apply config has been clicked.
help.errors_4: Combinations do not work: join with +, e.g. key:ctrl+shift+t; do not write key:ctrl shift t or key:ctrl+alt t.
help.errors_5: Input lands somewhere else: the page has not loaded yet; raise wait: (e.g. wait:2000).
help.errors_6: The target app receives nothing: when it runs as administrator, the host must run as administrator too.
help.errors_7: No effect on Linux / macOS: keyboard needs root (sudo python app.py); if you cannot elevate, use Run command instead.
help.errors_8: The URL does not open: url: must be followed by http:// or https://.
help.errors_9: The chosen browser is ignored: browser: only accepts chrome / firefox / edge / safari / default; an unknown or missing browser is logged with the reason, the URL opens in the default browser and the macro continues.
help.example_app_1: After launching the app, app: waits for its window to get focus (up to 3 s on Windows, no wait on macOS/Linux) and then runs the following text: / key: / paste: steps. When the app starts slowly, add a wait: as a safety margin; when the executable does not exist the log says "app: executable … was not found" and skips the step while the rest of the macro keeps running.
help.example_app_2: Quotes in the arguments may sit anywhere (app:C:\app.exe --title="My App" is a single argument --title=My App); single quotes work too (app:'/usr/bin/foo'). Unbalanced quotes launch nothing: the log says "app: unbalanced quotes in the command line" and skips the step.
help.example_browser_1: browser: only affects the url: steps after it and may appear anywhere in the macro; without it the system default browser is used. Wait for the page to load before sending keys, otherwise they land in the address bar or another window.
help.h_example_app: Full example: launch a desktop app and type into it
help.h_example_browser: Full example: open a page in Chrome and sign in
help.h_password: What to do when password fields ignore input
help.keys_1: Key names are case-insensitive; write the name shown in the UI (PageUp and pageup are the same).
help.keys_13: Passed through to the keyboard library (the deck's default key codes are F13–F22)
help.keys_6: Home, End, Page Up, Page Down
help.keys_8: Left / right Ctrl (ctrl means left Ctrl)
help.macro_1: Choose Macro as the button's Host action and write one step per line; they run in order. Click Apply config in the top-right corner when done. Macros run on the host only — the deck still sends its HID key (unless that key is set to No key).
help.macro_10: Open a URL: uses the browser from a preceding browser:, otherwise the default one; it waits for the browser window to come to the front (up to 3 s on Windows, no wait on macOS/Linux) before the next step
help.macro_11: Launch a desktop application (executable path with optional arguments; quote paths or arguments that contain spaces, and quotes may sit anywhere in an argument, e.g. --title="My App"); PATH program names such as app:notepad and environment variables such as app:%LOCALAPPDATA%\App\app.exe work too; on Windows it waits up to 3 s for the app window to come to the front, on macOS/Linux it does not wait and the following text: / key: / paste: steps type straight into it
help.macro_13: Treated as key:, e.g. a bare enter line
help.macro_14: The log records only the step types of a macro, never the body of text: / paste:.
help.macro_4: Send one key or a combination; join modifiers with +, e.g. key:ctrl+alt+t
help.macro_5: Type text character by character, 20 ms apart by default
help.macro_6: Same, but with 80 ms between characters (text! followed by the delay in ms); raise it when characters are dropped
help.macro_7: Put the text on the clipboard and send Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on macOS): the first choice for Chinese text, special symbols and password fields where text: never lands
help.macro_9: Choose which browser the following url: steps use: chrome / firefox / edge / safari / default (case-insensitive); falls back to the default browser when it is not installed
help.password_1: Password fields (and the email field on a login page) are where keys get sent but no text appears. The macro itself does not fail, so work out which case applies and change the syntax.
help.password_10: Add wait:1500 for the page to load, then focus fields one by one with key:tab; after url: the browser window is brought to the front automatically (up to 3 s)
help.password_12: Chinese text, emoji or symbols such as @ # ¥ turn into other characters or disappear
help.password_13: Use paste: (the clipboard bypasses the keyboard layout), or switch to an English input method before text:
help.password_15: The macro works everywhere except that one app
help.password_16: Windows UIPI drops synthetic input from a lower-privilege process and there is no code-level workaround: run the host as administrator (right-click BindDeckLite.exe → Run as administrator)
help.password_18: Neither keys nor text: do anything, but typing by hand works
help.password_19: The app checks the LLKHF_INJECTED flag. Try paste: first (it sends one Ctrl+V, which many apps allow); if that fails it is a hard block
help.password_21: Fails only in password fields; normal fields work
help.password_22: Secure keyboard entry blocks synthetic keys. Use paste:, or temporarily turn secure keyboard entry off in the input menu
help.password_23: Browser password field not rendered yet
help.password_24: The first few keys are lost, later ones work
help.password_25: Raise wait: to 2000 or more; repeat key:tab if needed
help.password_26: Recommended: wait: first, focus with key:tab, then use paste: for both the account and the password.
help.password_27: Administrator apps: when the target runs as administrator (Task Manager, some banking or game clients), the host must run as administrator too, otherwise no key scheme works.
help.password_28: Cases with no workaround: bank security controls, synthetic-input filtering inside remote desktop or virtual machines, clients with anti-cheat or active defence, and the UAC prompt itself. Use the deck's own HID keys, or type by hand.
help.password_29: Clipboard: paste: saves the text currently on the clipboard and restores it about 0.4 s after the paste (text only — images and other content cannot be restored). The password briefly sits on the clipboard during that window; when paste: is unavailable the log says "clipboard unavailable" and the step falls back to typing, so the macro does not stop.
help.password_30: Linux / macOS: macOS uses the built-in pbcopy; Linux prefers xclip / xsel (X11) or wl-copy (Wayland) and falls back to tkinter, which needs a graphical session (DISPLAY).
help.password_6: Only a few characters land, in the wrong order; the log says the action succeeded
help.password_7: Slow it down with text!80:password, or use paste:password
help.password_8: Focus is not in the field
help.password_9: Text lands in the address bar, the search box or another window

ui.sleep_hint: The wake inputs above are authoritative: on a classic ESP32, default layout, only the first wake-capable key wakes the deck on its own and the other RTC keys must be held together (ext1 needs every selected pin low at once); on an ESP32-C3 any key on GPIO0–5 wakes it alone.
